endpoints.name: firmware_info
endpoints.notes: Form body appid=141&project_no=TR2302_1248_ble&version=<int> (version must be an integer, built from the major/minor digits; the server enforces a floor — version=1 returns "no data", ~100+ works). Exercised live 2026-08-18: returned version_no 101 with a downloadable .ufw on images.heaton.com.cn (see sources). Unauthenticated; the server answers unsigned requests with a browser-like User-Agent (bare curl gets an nginx 403), images download only with Referer: https://manage.heaton.com.cn/, and the server rate-limits aggressively (HTTP 429 after ~100 rapid queries; ~5 s spacing works). A systematic 2026-08-19 harvest confirmed appid 141 serves exactly two projects: TR2302_1248_ble (the same v101 image) and TR2411R015_000102_mcu (see the second firmware_image source). A staging host tmanage.heaton.com.cn is also referenced in the app.
endpoints.returns: JSON: need_update, force, desc_cn/desc_en, version_no, file_path

cloud.failure_mode: Loss of the preset material library (cloud-hosted pattern/animation downloads) and of firmware-update checks. Everything else — DIY images/animations/text, programs, brightness, power, turn signals, timers, screen mirroring, the handlebar remote — is local BLE and keeps working. The panel itself has no radio but BLE and never contacts the cloud directly.
cloud.notes: The device is BLE-only; only the companion app talks to these hosts. Whether the app uploads telemetry or account data was not audited. Firmware and material files are served from https://images.heaton.com.cn/uploads/… .

identity.notes: BLE address type (public vs random-static) is unverified; if the address rotates, re-resolve by scanning for the name prefix / FA02 characteristic.

ble.notes: Name prefix is an app-code constant pending on-air confirmation. Fallback: connect and enumerate — the command characteristic 0000fa02-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb (and the JieLi OTA service 0000ae00-…) identify this family regardless of the advertised name.

identification.notes: The advertising name prefix TR2023-1248 is a string constant in the app, unconfirmed on-air. The JieLi OTA service 0000ae00-… comes from the bundled JieLi SDK constants; whether it appears in the advertisement (as opposed to the GATT table after connect) is unknown. The app discovers services dynamically and matches the command channel by characteristic UUID 0000fa02-…, so clients should do the same rather than trusting a containing-service UUID.

device.manufacturer: TIRO Innovation Technology (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd. (OEM; sold under dozens of storefront brands)
device.name: Smart LED Helmet Display (TIRO/Heaton)
device.notes:
Generic OEM Bluetooth RGB LED matrix panel (12x48 pixels, per the firmware project name TR2302_1248_ble) that straps onto a bicycle or motorcycle helmet: handlebar remote, turn-signal display fed by an accelerometer in the panel, speedometer ("ride info"), DIY image/animation/text upload, music-rhythm (mic) mode, daily on/off timers. Sold on Amazon/AliExpress/Shopify under many brand names (listings variously say Dpofirs, OPPWONG, Gelrova, YouRfocus, PChero, Masdio and others); current listings instruct buyers to install the "Shining Display" app.
COMPANION APP: "Shining Display" for Android (~27K Play downloads; developer listed as TIRO INNOVATION TECHNOLOGY (SHENZHEN) CO., LTD., tiro.cc — company alive, site live 2026-08-18). The app is React Native; all protocol logic is in the Hermes bundle. Internal product-type string translates to "helmet screen". Device/project identifiers found in the app: advertising-name prefix TR2023-1248, OTA project_no TR2302_1248_ble, a second variant pair TR2411R015_000102_ble / TR2411R015_000102_mcu (dual BLE+MCU OTA project, possibly a newer revision — unverified).
HARDWARE PLATFORM: JieLi BLE SoC. The app bundles the JieLi OTA SDK (com.jieli.jl_bt_ota) plus a TIRO wrapper (com.tiro.jlotalibrary); firmware images use the JieLi .ufw format (JLUFW update containers with plaintext section strings: JLUFW, JLBTSDK, btstack, ble_ota.bin / ble_app_ota.bin). SoC MIGRATION OBSERVED: the older helmet image TR2306R009-2.ufw (2024-03, for project TR2302_1248_ble) targets AC632N (BR22 platform), while the newer TR2411R014-02.ufw (fetched 2026-08-19 for the TR2411R015_000102_mcu project, changelog dated 2025-01-07) carries AC695x / BR22 markers — Heaton moved this product line from AC632N to AC695N during 2024. That newer image embeds the internal project string hTR2306R004 and is the MCU-companion half of the dual BLE+MCU OTA project, which is therefore confirmed to be a newer hardware revision, not just a variant code.
FAMILY BOUNDARY — do not conflate. Two older/other "LED helmet display" ecosystems exist: (1) the LOY family (LOY PLAY com.yskj.loy / LOY EYES com.yskj.lysd, Shenzhen Yanse, BLE service FFF0, popled.cn cloud) — a different OEM with a different protocol; (2) the Shining Mask / Shining Glasses / Magic Display family (Quintic QPP platform, AES-128-ECB encrypted 16-byte ASCII commands; see shining-mask.yaml, shining-glasses.yaml, magic-display.yaml) — also different despite the overlapping seller/developer names ("tirohk"). THIS spec covers only the TIRO/Heaton JieLi-based panel driven by the Shining Display app, identified by the FA02 command characteristic. Unlike the Quintic family, no encryption or pairing was found anywhere in the command path — plain GATT writes.
CLOUD: backend operated by Heaton (manage.heaton.com.cn / images.heaton.com.cn, both alive 2026-08-18; the same backend serves sibling apps Magic Display and Magical LED). The device itself is BLE-only and never touches the internet — only the phone app does, and only for the preset material library and OTA checks. See the cloud block.
CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM for the GATT layout (FA02 write, JieLi AE00/AE01/ AE02 OTA service) and the command table — read straight out of the app's builder functions, but not exercised on hardware. LOW for the advertising name prefix (code constant, needs an on-air scan), the flag-byte semantics, the direction value map, and everything about the bulk pixel/program upload pipeline beyond the dispatch-function names.

credentials.notes: No credentials of any kind: the panel is BLE-only and the command path carries no authentication.

factory_reset.effect: App exposes a "reset device" command (reset_device below, opcode 0x03 flag 0x80, no payload). What it actually clears — user programs, name, timers — is inferred from the UI label, not observed; no hardware button procedure was found in listings or the app.

steps.action: Write the reset_device frame (04 00 03 80) to the FA02 characteristic.
steps.notes: App-derived only; behaviour on the panel (reboot, LED signal, what survives) is unverified.

ble.pin_source: None — plain GATT writes, no bonding seen in the app's command path.

methods.description: Scan for the TR2023-1248 name prefix, connect, enumerate services, and locate the FA02 write characteristic and the JieLi AE02 notify characteristic. No pairing/bonding or encryption appears anywhere in the app's command path.

steps.action: Power on the helmet display panel.
steps.expect: Panel advertises with a TR2023-1248-prefixed name (app-code constant; confirm on-air).

steps.action: Connect and discover services; find the characteristic 0000fa02-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb by UUID.
Enable notifications on 0000ae02-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb (JieLi OTA service) — the app does this at connect time and receives command ACKs / disconnect events there.
Negotiate MTU (the app reacts to the negotiated MTU and chunks large writes to fit).
Optionally sync the clock (sync_time command). The app sends it on connect; whether the panel requires it before accepting other commands is unverified.

setup.notes: Nothing to provision: no Wi-Fi, no account, no cloud. Power the panel on, scan, connect. App-derived, not replayed on hardware.

rejoin.notes: No network to rebind. The usual connection failure is another central still holding the link — close the vendor app before connecting from another client.

testing.notes: Everything here comes from static analysis of the companion app ("Shining Display", whose protocol logic lives in a React Native Hermes bundle) and live probes of the vendor cloud API on 2026-08-18. No BLE traffic was captured and no hardware was driven; the command frames below are read out of the app's command-builder functions, not replayed against a panel.

entities.name: Display Power
entities.notes: Write-only channel, and deliberately so: no entity here binds state_characteristic because the command channel 0000fa02 is write-only — a consumer honouring that field would issue a read or a CCCD subscribe and get ATT 0x02 / 0x0E — and the device's only notify characteristic, 0000ae02, is the JieLi OTA channel, which carries no entity state. There is no state readback to offer, so a consumer must track what it sent.

entities.name: Turn Signal Direction
entities.notes: Six raw indices 0-5; the index-to-direction map is unverified.

entities.name: Gesture Sensing
entities.notes: Shares opcode 0x0B with the mic command, selected by flag byte 0x01. Write-only channel; no state readback is documented, so a consumer must track what it sent.

entities.name: Voice Activation
entities.notes: Write-only channel; no state readback is documented, so a consumer must track what it sent.

covers: display power, brightness, text scroll speed
turn-signal direction display and gesture/voice switches
DIY image/animation/text upload, programs/playlists, daily on/off timers, screen mirroring (byte-level formats partially untraced — see remaining_unknowns)
not_covered: firmware update checks and image hosting (cloud-hosted; a captured .ufw can in principle be flashed without the cloud via the JieLi OTA service)
local_access.summary: The panel speaks plain unauthenticated BLE GATT as shipped; the cloud is an optional content store, not a control path. A minimal client is ~5-byte writes to characteristic FA02 (e.g. from bleak).

remaining_unknowns: Flag byte (offset 3) semantics: 0x01 vs 0x80 looks like a sub-command selector sharing opcodes; verify on-air
Direction command value map (indices 0-5 to off/left/right/hazard/brake)
Advertising name prefix TR2023-1248 needs an on-air scan; the containing service UUID of FA02 is unpinned (app matches by characteristic)

Pixel/program upload byte-level formats: getSendData pipeline, 12x48 RGB packing, sendTool_sendDiyData / sendPicWithData / sendTextData / sendWordData / sendTool_sendPraseModle / sendClockModel / sendTool_toupingWithData dispatch functions identified but not fully traced
Device-to-app feedback format on AE02 (ACKs; battery? handlebar-remote button events?)

Whether TR2411R015_000102_ble/mcu (dual BLE+MCU OTA project) is a newer helmet revision — RESOLVED 2026-08-19: its MCU-companion image TR2411R014-02.ufw carries AC695x/BR22 markers vs the older panel image's AC632N, so it is a newer (2025) hardware revision on the AC695N SoC
FCC ID unknown (no listing carries one; Chinese SRRC CMIIT ID may be on the hardware label)
JieLi .ufw decryption (chip-series key) if firmware internals are wanted

ota_start.advanced_reason: Starts a firmware update session on the JieLi OTA service. An interrupted or wrong-image update can leave the panel unbootable; only proceed with a known-good .ufw for this exact project (TR2302_1248_ble).
ota_start.description: Begin firmware update: 0xAA opcode with flag 0x55, then JieLi OTA data flows over AE01/AE02

v.notes: Payload byte meaning not traced (possibly a mode or image-slot selector).

reset_device.advanced_reason: Resets the panel; user programs, schedules and settings are presumed lost (the exact effect is unverified). Recovery is re-sending your configuration from a client.

level.notes: Raw byte; the app's UI scale-to-wire mapping was not traced.

direction.notes: UI index 0-5. The index-to-meaning map (off / left / right / hazard / brake / ?) is NOT verified — the six values come from the app's direction picker; capture or hardware test needed.

set_gesture_switch.description: Gesture-sensing switch (shares opcode 0x0B with the mic command, selected by flag byte 0x01)

set_mic.description: Microphone / music-rhythm mode command (6-byte frame; 2 payload bytes, meanings not traced)

set_ride_info.description: Send ride-info / speedometer data (3 payload bytes; byte meanings — speed encoding, units — not traced)

set_text_speed.description: Set text scroll speed (shares opcode 0x03 with reset, selected by flag byte 0x01)

speed.notes: Range/stepping unverified — the app builder takes a single byte.

sync_time.description: Sync time/date to the panel (7 payload bytes built by the app's getDateInfo helper). The field layout of the 7 payload bytes (year/month/day/hour/minute/second/weekday packing) was not traced out of the helper — capture on hardware before relying on this.

characteristics.name: Display Command
characteristics.notes:
All display commands are raw byte arrays written here. Frame layout recovered from the app's command builders:

  byte 0: total frame length N (covers the whole frame)
  byte 1: 0x00
  byte 2: command opcode
  byte 3: flag byte — 0x01 or 0x80 observed on ordinary
          commands, 0x55 on the OTA-start command
  byte 4..: payload

The flag byte at offset 3 appears to act as a sub-command selector sharing opcodes (0x03 flag 0x80 = factory reset vs 0x03 flag 0x01 = text scroll speed; 0x0B flag 0x01 = gesture switch vs 0x0B flag 0x80 = microphone/music-rhythm) — HYPOTHESIS, verify on-air. The app negotiates MTU and chunks large payloads to the negotiated limit (its limitLength / cutArray helpers); bulk visual data (DIY canvas, image/text upload, playlists, screen mirroring) uses the same length-prefixed framing chunked by MTU, but the byte-level bitmap packing (12x48 RGB layout, getSendData pipeline) was not fully traced — see remaining_unknowns. No response is read back on this characteristic; device-to-app feedback arrives as AE02 notifications on the JieLi OTA service.

services.name: Helmet Display Command Service
services.notes: CONTAINING SERVICE UUID UNKNOWN — this entry's UUID is a stand-in equal to the command characteristic's. The app never pins the service: it enumerates all services and selects the characteristic 0000fa02-… by UUID (the bundled JieLi SDK likewise binds AE00 by constant). A full string-table sweep of the app's Hermes bundle (17,247 strings) finds exactly one 16-bit-based vendor UUID, FA02. Clients MUST locate the characteristic by enumeration, not by this service UUID, and MUST NOT match this entry as a service.

characteristics.name: JieLi OTA Write
characteristics.notes: OTA data channel. Wire format is the JieLi OTA protocol's own (SDK-internal), not traced here.

characteristics.name: JieLi OTA Notify
characteristics.notes: OTA result channel, and the app's general device-to-app feedback path (command ACKs, disconnect events). Payload format unknown — whether battery level or handlebar-remote button events also surface here is an open question.

services.name: JieLi OTA Service
services.notes: Standard JieLi (jl_bt_ota SDK) firmware-update service. UUIDs come from the SDK's BluetoothConstant class bundled in the app. The app enables AE02 notifications at connect time and also routes ordinary command ACKs / disconnect events through it (via the BLE-manager characteristic-updated event), so AE02 is worth subscribing to even when not updating firmware. Firmware images are JieLi .ufw (JLUFW) containers with plaintext section strings. Live images for both known OTA projects were fetched from the vendor cloud (see sources).

sources.description: Static analysis of the "Shining Display" Android companion app (2026-08-18). It is a React Native build: all protocol logic lives in its Hermes bytecode bundle, which was disassembled in full (string table plus code) to recover the command builders. The Java side contributed the JieLi OTA UUIDs AE00/AE01/AE02 and the OEM's wrapper around the JieLi OTA SDK.

Panel firmware version_no 101 (changelog 'Fix bug', dated 2024-03-21), 512,256 bytes, fetched live from the vendor API 2026-08-18. JieLi JLUFW update container (plaintext section strings JLUFW / JLBTSDK / ble_ota.bin); strings triage places it on the AC632N (BR22) platform.

TR2411R014-02.ufw — MCU-companion firmware for the dual BLE+MCU OTA project TR2411R015_000102_mcu (appid 141, queried at version 202; changelog dated 2025-01-07, 'Modified the default brightness'), fetched live 2026-08-19 during a systematic harvest of the vendor OTA API. JLUFW container with AC695x / BR22 markers (JieLi AC695N — the line migrated from AC632N during 2024); embeds the internal project string hTR2306R004. Archived locally with checksums alongside the rest of that harvest (referenced, not committed).
Sibling-family (Shining Mask) open client — confirms the broader product family's design patterns; the helmet panel itself shows NO encryption in its command path.

Same-family and adjacent companion apps looked at for comparison (2026-08-18): Magic Display, Magical LED, iPixel Pro and SDJ from the same OEM, plus the LOY PLAY / LOY EYES pair. Only skimmed, not analysed in depth; the LOY apps were confirmed to be a different OEM family from their bundled JS assets.
